findings.claim: An uncalibrated two-phase carbon-density mixture improves transfer to unseen countries over simple controls.
findings.evidence: Development MAE 0.260 g/cm³ selected this model, but reserved MAE 0.336 exceeds the constant control 0.173, linear 0.313 and flexible 0.315.
findings.known_prior_art: Organic/mineral volume mixing and carbon-based pedotransfer are established.
findings.falsification: Strong underprediction in Germany; worst-country MAE 0.608 g/cm³.
findings.scope: Four development countries and two held-out countries; no target calibration.

findings.claim: Development-selected carbon-only mixing does not provide reliable country transfer for this complete-case cohort.
findings.equation: Comparison of frozen mixture with country-balanced mean-density baseline.
findings.evidence: Both confirmation countries retained. Mixture reserved MAE 0.336 versus baseline 0.173 g/cm³; no post-confirmation reselection.
findings.known_prior_art: Bulk density reflects mineralogy, structure, compaction and measurement protocol as well as carbon.
findings.falsification: This does not imply no carbon-density relationship within a site.
findings.scope: Water-pH eligibility removes UK and Netherlands; remaining countries are not a representative random sample.

findings.claim: The tested depth and acidity mechanisms do not repair the development transfer limitation.
findings.equation: Depth-dependent mineral packing, organic consolidation and pH-dependent packing alternatives in rules.json.
findings.evidence: All four mechanistic extensions have worse held-country development MAE than the two-phase mixture; their confirmation results remain available.
findings.known_prior_art: Compaction and soil aggregation are established processes; these simple proxies are insufficient here.
findings.falsification: No causal effect of depth or pH is estimated, and no missing texture is imputed.

scientific_adjudication: Agent-assisted analysis; not independent experimental replication or human expert adjudication.
